(i) **Monomers:**
- **Definition:** Small, reactive, low-molecular-weight molecules that can chemically react with each other or other molecules to form a large chain-like macromolecule (polymer).
- **Example:** Ethylene ($CH_2=CH_2$), which polymerizes to form polyethylene.

(ii) **Functionality:**
- **Definition:** The number of reactive bonding sites or functional groups per molecule of a monomer that can participate in polymerization reactions.
- **Example:** Ethylene has a functionality of 2 (can react from both ends), whereas glycerol has a functionality of 3.

(iii) **Polymer:**
- **Definition:** A large macromolecule built up by linking together a large number of small repeating units (monomers) through covalent bonds.
- **Example:** Polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyethylene, or nylon.
proTip: Functionality determines whether a polymer will form linear chains (functionality = 2) or cross-linked networks (functionality > 2).
